hints.title: Find the limits from the curve
hints.body: A turning point of a differentiable polynomial has zero gradient. Differentiate the given cubic and solve for the two stationary inputs.
hints.recap: Stationary points can supply limits that are not given explicitly.
hints.pitfall: Use the input coordinates of the turning points, not their heights.
hints.pause: Find both inputs and order them to identify the lower and upper limits.

recall.reminder: Stationary points can supply limits that are not given explicitly.

hints.title: Keep the integral signed
hints.body: Integrate each term using the power rule, then evaluate the antiderivative at your upper and lower limits.
hints.recap: A definite integral is the upper antiderivative value minus the lower one.
hints.pitfall: The expression asks for a signed integral; do not split it into unsigned areas.
hints.pause: Find the antiderivative and substitute both limits, keeping brackets around each evaluation.

recall.reminder: A definite integral is the upper antiderivative value minus the lower one.

hints.title: Check for cancellation
hints.body: If your limits have equal magnitude and opposite signs, compare the even-power and odd-power terms in the antiderivative.
hints.recap: Even powers take the same value at opposite inputs; odd powers change sign.
hints.pitfall: Subtracting the lower-limit bracket changes every sign inside that bracket.
hints.pause: Use the symmetry to simplify the difference you have obtained.

recall.reminder: Even powers take the same value at opposite inputs; odd powers change sign.

solution:
1. Locate the turning points. The derivative is 3x2−6. Setting it to zero gives x2=2, so α=−2 and β=2. The derivative is positive outside these roots and negative between them, so both are turning points.

2. Integrate the polynomial. An antiderivative is F(x)=x44−3x2+3x. Therefore the required integral is F(2)−F(−2).

3. Subtract the endpoint values. The even-power terms cancel, leaving 32−(−32)=62.

Answer F. The symmetry also shows that the odd part x3−6x contributes zero over these limits.
knowledgePattern: Differentiate to find integration bounds, then integrate a cubic on symmetric limits
